edits.text: Adapt to directed weighted graphs by using Dijkstra's algorithm with proper edge direction handling. When the graph is undirected, mirror edges in both directions. Always handle self-loop and duplicate edge constraints per input specification. Use adjacency lists for efficient traversal and standard priority queue for shortest path computation.

Parse the graph type (directed/undirected) and weight status to construct appropriate adjacency representation. For directed graphs, maintain one-way edges; for undirected, add reverse edge with same weight. Implement Dijkstra's algorithm with early termination on path discovery when applicable. Ensure correct initialization of distances and priority queue handling.

Iterative refinement focuses on correctness for directed graphs, where edge directionality must be respected. Initial versions with undirected assumptions fail when input is actually directed; subsequent iterations fix this by dynamically adjusting adjacency construction based on graph type.
